name: Riwaq Court
summary: A square minaret rises from the exact meeting point of two deep prayer-hall wings, leaving an open courtyard.
why: Two perpendicular wings use common screen axes (1, 0.5) and (-1, 0.5). Their roof is one continuous L at z=12. The tower grows directly from the joined rear corner; the doorway is projected on its own wall plane.
risk: The architecture emphasizes a North African courtyard mosque rather than a familiar onion-dome outline. The courtyard remains especially clear in the monochrome mark.
reasonToChoose: You want an architectural mosque identity with visible depth and a distinct courtyard silhouette.
